issue_context.title: ConfigurationBinder fails to set values for properties of a type with ISet<T> variations
issue_context.body:
### Description

ConfigurationBinder throws an exception in curtain cases related to `ISet<T>` usages.
Exception message is:

```
Object of type 'System.Collections.Generic.List`1[System.String]' cannot be converted to type 'System.Collections.Generic.ISet`1[System.String]'.
```

So far I found these cases:

```cs
class MyOptions
{
    public ISet<string>? Prop1 { get; set; }

    public IDictionary<string, ISet<string>> Prop2 { get; set; } = new Dictionary<string, ISet<string>>();

    public IDictionary<string, ISet<string>>? Prop3 { get; set; }
}
```

### Reproduction Steps

I created a short repro: https://github.com/xakep139/config-binder-set-issue
In [`MyOptions`](https://github.com/xakep139/config-binder-set-issue/blob/master/ConsoleApp1/MyOptions.cs) class all properties that cause an exception are commented out, i.e.:

- `public ISet<string>? NullableSet { get; set; }`
- `public IDictionary<string, ISet<string>> AssignedISetDict { get; set; } = new Dictionary<string, ISet<string>>();`
- `public IDictionary<string, ISet<string>>? NullableISetDict { get; set; }`

### Expected behavior

No exception is thrown, values are bound as expected

### Actual behavior

The exception is thrown:

The `FindOpenGenericInterface` as currently used and implemented is busted. We should never try assigning a `List<string>` to an `ISet<string>` which will never work, but we currently attempt to because `ISet<T>` has an `ICollection<T>` implementation.

The current logic just assumes that any interface that implements `ICollection<T>` or `IEnumerable<T>` must be assignable from a `List<T>` which is simply not the case as this demonstrates. We have a similar issue with `IDictionary<TKey, TVaue>`.

Instead, we should check if `typeof(ISet<string>).IsAssignableFrom(typeof<List<string>>)`, `typeof(ISet<string>).IsAssignableFrom(typeof<HashSet<string>>)` (if we decide to support ISet) etc... It's a bit more complicated because of open generics and variable types, but that's the general idea.

Edit: This is where we're currently creating the `List<T>` that we're attempting to assign to the `ISet<T>`:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/8b42dffa5f37762caddbe949ebc2fc348cca5121/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.Binder/src/ConfigurationBinder.cs#L256-L263

@maryamariyan unfortunately, my current capacity doesn't allow me to implement the approach proposed by @halter73 right now.
Once I have a chance, will continue my work on this issue.
@maryamariyan - I'm happy to look at this. It's pretty similar to a few other PRs I've done in this area (I just hope one of them isn't the cause of this issue! 😅 )

PR #68133 fixes this issue. It can't fix the scenario where you have this in your options (from the example above):

`public IDictionary<string, ISet<string>> Prop2 { get; set; } = new Dictionary<string, ISet<string>>();`

It does, however, fix:

`public IDictionary<string, ISet<string>> Prop2 { get; set; }`

@SteveDunn thank you for your PR. However, it does mostly the same thing as mine #66151, thought it doesn't cover `IReadOnlySet` case (did I miss something?).
As far as I understand, folks want to have an implementation that @halter73 suggested - using `typeof(ISet<string>).IsAssignableFrom(typeof<Set<string>>)`

@xakep139 - yes, I noticed your PR immediately after committing mine! :) 

Mine now supports `IReadOnlySet`, but did involve a fair amount of head scratching to get it to work. I [added a local function](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/68133/files#diff-2e6f75e1d4f577e1c8c1b6a32d158ce7812a38ad8fcd3b4d762157b92c03e890R570-R586) to resolve the generic type for the new collection (`HashSet<>` or `List<>`) and used a `MethodInfo` to call the `Add` method. This was needed as there is no common type between `HashSet<>` and `List<>` that contains an `Add` method.
Well, I guess there's an `ICollection` that is common for both `HashSet` and `List` and it contains an `Add` method

Maybe, but I couldn't see one that was obvious (as obvious as the non
generic List at least)
